subject: Mutual success blueprint & exit-test inventory for Greenfield POC
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@greenfieldhealth.com>, Samir Rao <samir@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual success blueprint & exit-test inventory for Greenfield POC

Hi Elaine / Samir —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation, attached is a one-page mutual action blueprint (MAP) plus a compact exit-test inventory that ties acceptance tests directly to the go/no-go decision. High level:

- Goal: Validate that Redwood reduces inference latency 40% vs your current setup at 95th pct load while keeping hallucination rate under 2% on the clinical triage prompt set.
- Duration: 4-week pilot (2-week smoke + 2-week load/edge-case validation).
- Primary exit gates: latency SLO, concordance on top-3 intents, and SOC2 evidence review.
- Acceptance tests: sample prompts, throughput profile, KV-cache warmup scenarios, and deterministic seed checks for reranker.

Action items I recommend for this week:
1) Review attached MAP_v1 and highlight any missing success metrics by Wed EOD.
2) Karthik and Marissa will draft the concrete test harness and a short schedule for execution.
3) Procurement touchpoint for contract glidepath — Samir, would you introduce your procurement contact?

I put procurement steps at the bottom of the sheet; nothing binding, just to align expectations.

Attachments: 2027-05-16_MAP_v1.xlsx

Best,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Elaine Park <elaine@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual success blueprint & exit-test inventory for Greenfield POC

Jonas — thanks for the crisp summary and the MAP. Quick notes from our side:

- The latency target looks good but we need a complementary metric on 99th pct under sustained bursts (30s windows). Can you add that to the acceptance list?
- Security: we will need a completed security questionnaire before we run any live PHI traffic. Can Karthik fill out the GFH security checklist? I attached our questionnaire template.
- Procurement: forwarded this thread to procurement; they’ll request the SOW and pricing schedule. Expect an initial redline.

If those three items are addressed we can commit to the 4-week cadence.

Thanks,
Elaine
VP Product, Greenfield Health
Elaine.Park@greenfieldhealth.com

On Mon, May 16, 2027 at 09:12 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 May 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mutual success blueprint & exit-test inventory for Greenfield POC

Thanks Elaine — noted. I attached our filled security questionnaire and a proposed acceptance-test catalog that maps each test to a pass/fail criterion and the responsible owner. Quick summary of the acceptance catalog highlights:

- Latency: 95th pct < target (primary), 99th pct burst windows measured separately (secondary). Test harness uses synthetic traffic plus a small sample of de-identified prompts you provide.
- Quality: concordance on top-3 intents >= 94% (measured by label set you provide); hallucination threshold <= 2% on curated edge cases.
- Reliability: KV cache warmup behavior documented; cold-start and scale-up scenarios included.
- Data handling: all test traffic uses de-identified records; we will not store PHI.

Attachments: GFH_Security_Questionnaire_filled.pdf, Acceptance_Test_Catalog_v1.xlsx

Timeline suggestion:
- Week 0 (prep): finalize SOW and share de-identified prompt set (Elaine).
- Week 1: smoke tests and tuning (low volume).
- Week 2–3: load and edge-case validation.
- Week 4: consolidated results and decision meeting (red/amber/green).

I can incorporate the 99th pct burst windows into the latency tests — will add a dedicated check in the catalog.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
